tools.name: recall_memories
tools.description: Retrieve relevant memories about the user from CLS++ cross-LLM memory. Use this when the user asks about themselves, their preferences, past conversations, or when you need context from their other AI sessions (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.).

query.description: What to search for — user identity, preferences, recent work, relationships, etc.

limit.description: Max number of memories to return (default 5)

tools.name: store_memory
tools.description: Store a new fact about the user in CLS++ memory. Use this when the user shares personal information, preferences, decisions, or important context that should persist across AI sessions.

text.description: The fact to remember — e.g., 'User prefers dark mode', 'User's name is Raj'

tools.name: capture_conversation
tools.description: Capture the current conversation/session into CLS++ continuous memory. Use this at the end of a conversation, before handing off to another LLM, or whenever the user asks for this session to be remembered. Provide a concise summary, optional raw transcript, and durable facts/decisions so another connected LLM can hot-swap into the latest context.

summary.description: Concise session summary: what happened, decisions made, current state, blockers, and next steps.

transcript.description: Optional raw or compact transcript excerpt for exact continuity.

facts.description: Durable facts, preferences, product requirements, decisions, or commitments extracted from the conversation.

surface.description: Where the conversation happened, e.g. claude-web, cursor, claude-code, chatgpt.

tools.name: who_am_i
tools.description: Return everything CLS++ knows about the user — identity, preferences, relationships, recent activity. Use this at the start of a conversation or when the user asks 'what do you know about me?'
